sources.text: Our multimodal predictions are colored by log-likelihood (red: high, blue: low)Abstract Predicting the future motion of multiple people is inherently stochastic: the same observed history admits many plausible continuations depending on intent, coordination, and social context. Yet the dominant paradigm in multi-person 3D motion prediction remains deterministic, with existing methods producing a fixed number of outputs per agent. In contrast, we present a conditional flow matching framework that jointly generates diverse future motions for multiple agents, modeling both global trajectories and root-relative poses

sources.text: et al., 2023]. This leaves an open challenge for a unified generative frameworkWe address this challenge with a flow matching framework for multi-person 3D motion prediction. We decompose joint positions into a global root trajectory and root-relative local pose, modeling both within a shared generative model. Rather than generating every future frame independently, predictions are made in a compact B-spline control-point space, reducing integration cost while enforcing temporal smoothness

Contributions(i) On the base checkpoint 25.8% [22.9–28.7] of questions change their answer purely because the options were reordered (19.7% on the 605 English-language items alone). (ii) The dependence is not a first/last artefact alone: the first-vs-last accuracy gap is 10.1%, but predictions are concentrated in particular slots (total-variation distance from uniform 0.09 at K=3, 0.07 at K=12). (iii) Fine-tuning with shuffling reduces the flip rate to 7.2%, whereas the same rows without shuffling give 11.4%

Fine-tuning with shuffling (Maya-v1) lowers the ratio only to 2.2× and the no-shuffle ablation to 1.4×; the parallel layout brings it to 1.22× (essentially flat). This qualifies the headline result of the previous section: shuffled finetuning removes most content-dependent flips on realistic questions, but a latent position prior remains whenever the content is uninformative, and only the architectural change removes it

They are simple and publicly motivated, and we think measurement is more useful to defenders than harmful to them. 18  Conclusion Laya’s released checkpoints are order-sensitive on realistic questions: 25.8% of questions flip when only the option order changes. Data alone (shuffled fine-tuning on a few thousand teacher-verified rows) reduces this to 7.2%, and the no-shuffle ablation shows that the shuffling, not merely the rows, is responsible for 4.2% of it
